Source_3.value: Spaghetti linked to fatal human emetic foodborne illness case

Free_Text.value: Reportedly isolated from spaghetti linked to a fatal case of foodborne emetic intoxication on 1 October 2008 in Brussels, Belgium. A 20-year-old man died following the ingestion of pasta contaminated with Bacillus cereus. Emetic strains of B. cereus were isolated (9.5 × 10^7 CFU/g), and high levels of cereulide (14.8 μg/g) were found in the spaghetti meal. However, cereulide synthetase genes were not detected in this genome; further, this genome belongs to Group IV, incicating that this genome may not be responsible for the emetic illness.
